sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5,931.4 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
The shape is a decelerating growth curve: 64.2% in FY2021, 11.8% in FY2022, 0.1% in FY2023, then 16.4% and 10.6% in FY2024 and FY2025 [D218][D263][D311][D358][D406].
The FY2017 operating loss of $3,485.6 million reflected a $2.6 billion increase in stock-based compensation tied to the CEO award and IPO-condition RSUs [F12][P74].
The FY2022 reversal, with the operating loss widening 98.7% to $1,395.3 million, came from higher cost of revenue and operating expenses that outpaced revenue [F17][D264][P42].
North America remains the largest market at 58.6% of FY2025 revenue but contributed only 4.4pp of the 10.6% growth [D456][D458][D406].
Other Revenue grew 62.9% in FY2025 and contributed 5.4pp, nearly matching advertising's 5.3pp on a 5.8% increase [D544][D545][D537][D538].
Advertising growth came from roughly 17% more impressions, led by Sponsored Snaps and Spotlight, partly offset by a 10% lower cost per impression; other revenue rose on subscription growth [P24].
Operating costs grew 5.5pp slower than revenue in FY2025, at 5.1%, and incremental operating margin was 44.8% [D430][D423][D429].
The diluted share count rose 2.1% in FY2025 while the net loss shrank 34.0%, so the loss per share fell 35.7% [D425][D408][D410].
The FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% is the window high, against a median of -32.4% and a low of -422.5% in FY2017 [F30][D554][D555][D553].
The FY2025 margin improved 5.7pp, with cost of revenue adding 1.1pp, R&D 1.3pp and other lines 3.3pp [D419][D431][D432][D433].
Sales and marketing fell $42.4 million on the timing of marketing events and lower advertising, while R&D rose $101.9 million on product development headcount [P22][P23].
In FY2025 net margin of -7.8% sat 1.2pp above the -9.0% operating margin, helped by $68.9 million of other income [F50][F30][X130].
Operating cash flow of $656.2 million in FY2025 exceeded the $460.5 million net loss, and free cash flow reached $437.2 million, a 7.4% margin [F80][F40][F100][D393].
Operating cash flow was driven by the net loss adjusted for $1.0 billion of stock-based compensation and $163.6 million of D&A [P13].
Capex of $219.0 million was 3.7% of revenue and 1.34x D&A [F90][D392][D395].
Capex in both years was primarily improvements to leased facilities to support team workspaces [P10].
Net cash of -$596.3 million in FY2025 is net debt, down from $1,439.8 million of net cash in FY2021 [D399][D211].
Net cash of -10.1% of revenue ranks at the 0th percentile against an internet peer median of 45.0% (n=5) [D400][D578][D579].
The company issued $1.50 billion of 2033 Notes and repurchased $1.4 billion of 2026-2028 notes in February 2025 [P2][P1].
Buybacks of $750.9 million were 171.7% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count still rose 2.1% [D401][D402][D425].
The company has posted a net loss in each of the last 10 years, from $514.6 million in FY2016 to $460.5 million in FY2025 [R1][F31][F40].
The loss is narrowing but ten straight years of red ink leave no demonstrated path to profitability [R1].
Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of revenue in FY2025 and at least 10% in each of the last 9 years [R2][D390].
Compensation equal to 191.1% of the operating loss means reported losses understate the cash-equivalent cost of the workforce [D404].
Net cash fell for four straight years into net debt of $596.3 million in FY2025 [R3][D399].
The shift from a cash cushion to net debt removes the buffer that funded past losses [R3].
Whether the FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% holds or improves will show in the FY2026 10-K [F30].
Whether net cash of -10.1% of revenue narrows or deepens will show in the FY2026 10-K [D400].
Whether stock-based compensation stays below the FY2025 level of 17.1% of revenue will show in the FY2026 10-K [D390].
